free_tier.stated: No published byte limit; AWS pays S3 storage plus egress and cross-region fees for the approved dataset, in a dedicated Program Account joined to AWS's billing organisation. 2-year term from the Effective Date, auto-terminates, extendable only if AWS offers. Rolling review, decision generally within two weeks.

per_object_cap.stated: no per-object cap was extracted from the seed's quota and limits prose; absence here is a gap in this conversion, not a vendor claim that no cap exists
per_object_cap.notes: extraction found no per-object clause; some of these providers meter on object count rather than bytes, and some state no cap

retention.stated: 90-day wind-down with data retrieval after termination.

egress.terms: Fully covered, including cross-region data fees - the only candidate in this slot with genuinely uncapped free egress at any volume.

tooling: Plain S3: aws-cli, boto3, s3fs, rclone 's3'; CloudFormation template from the onboarding handbook creates the public-read bucket with intelligent tiering and logging.
chaining: Per dataset, per dedicated account; the application form itself asks only for 'Name of your institution', dataset size and growth rate in GB/year - there is no upper bound field. Multiply by separate applications for separate datasets.

limits_note: THE BLOCKER: 'The signatory should be an authorized representative of your organization who has the authority to agree to legal terms on its behalf', and the application asks for institution name plus institution website. Requirements: permissive licence only (CC BY-NC and BY-ND barred), cloud-optimised formats, docs, a tutorial notebook, a Registry YAML PR, demonstrated community demand, and the account must run no other AWS services. 90-day wind-down with data retrieval after termination.
reliability_note: Production S3, no reliability concerns. Failure mode is review + the 2-year clock: a dataset that stops growing does not get renewed and the bill reverts to you.

extras.agent_focus: Bulk data programmes that pay for your storage. Two halves: (1) institutional/gov repositories and cloud open-data sponsorships, judged as free byte pools; (2) research grants that could fund storage for an unaffiliated individual. Revisited AWS ODS, Google Cloud public datasets, Source Cooperative. Central question for each: what is the unit of quota (account / record / dataset / collection / project), because that unit is the multiplier.

binding_note: the quota is real and unreachable: identity is the binding constraint, and it is not one of the six limits kinds
